text:
jun: heads-up — nightly probe picked up a regression for candidate_v3 on h100 at mid seqlens (128-512). saw token/s drop ~18% vs candidate_v2. perf-bot posted the summary below.
perf-bot: nightly-run #7831: candidate_v3 — h100 — summary -> throughput delta: -18% (128..512), p95 latency +22ms, KV-cache path exercised. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/7831 :eyes:
mike: Ugh. Is this reproducible locally or noisy on infra?
jun: fairly stable across 3 different workers. attached microbench traces in CI artifacts. quick grep from the log:
```
[2025-11-12T03:12:11Z] seq=256 kernel=candidate_v3 kv_cache=on batch=8 tokens/s=4200
[2025-11-12T03:12:12Z] seq=64  kernel=candidate_v3 kv_cache=on batch=8 tokens/s=4800
[2025-11-12T03:12:13Z] seq=512 kernel=candidate_v3 kv_cache=on batch=8 tokens/s=4100
[2025-11-12T03:12:14Z] seq=256 kernel=candidate_v2 kv_cache=on batch=8 tokens/s=5100
```
ria: looks like candidate_v3 has a poor mid-seq path when KV cache is hot. maybe the autotuner is picking a slower GEMM/kernel variant for those de-facto padded sizes.
sam: could be a vectorization mismatch or different k-splitting causing extra memcpy for certain seqlens. do we have perf counters for tile occupancy?
mike: can anyone run the microprobe locally? here's the quick repro command I used in CI — runs fast:
```
./microprobe --kernel candidate_v3 --arch h100 --seqs 64,128,256,512 --kv-cache on --batch 8 --iters 200 --log csv --out repro.csv
```
jun: confirmed — repro works. I also toggled kv-cache off and candidate_v3 matches v2 numbers. so KV codepath interaction is likely.
ria: short-term mitigation: add an autotune override to prefer candidate_v2 for h100 when seq in [128,512]. long-term: find why candidate_v3 kernel picks slower plan when kv_cache=true.
sam: agreed. I'll sketch an autotune rule. suggestion (pseudo-config):
```
{"rule": "prefer_candidate_v2_midseq",
 "if": {"arch": "h100", "min_seq": 128, "max_seq": 512, "kv_cache": true},
 "prefer": "candidate_v2"
}
```
mike: pls don't forget we need the nightly CI to gate this too — otherwise we ship with a perf regression. who will own the PR?
jun: I can own the PR for the autotuner override + add a small nightly microprobe test that exercises seq 128/256/512 with KV cache enabled.
mike: awesome. sam can you run a quick L2/SM metric capture on your node to see if there's a bandwidth/memory-stall signal? use nvprof/nsys and the microprobe flags.
sam: yep, will run and paste results. expect a 30-40min run. ping me if you want raw traces.
perf-bot: scheduled: nightly-gate added -> microprobe.kv-midseq test will run in the 02:00 UTC sweep starting tomorrow. CI link for gating: https://ci.redwood.internal/suites/microprobe.kv-midseq
deploy-bot: note — adding autotune overrides requires config eval + release notes. please add a CHANGELOG entry in the PR.
jun: noted. plan timeline: PR with rule + test today, sam posts perf counters tomorrow, follow-up issue to root-cause the kernel's vectorization decisions. cc @mike @ria @sam :thumbsup:
mike: thanks. if anyone sees regressions for other arches (ampere/hopper) call it out, but start with h100 since that's where delta is biggest.
ria: logging follow-up: i'll add a short smoke that toggles kv-cache on/off and compares candidate_v2/v3 in the nightly report so we get automatic diffs.
jun: thanks all, will post PR link when ready.
